tagline: Up the James from the cannon works to the Huguenot chapel.
intro: From Route 147 in Richmond, Old Gun Road, Robious Road and Huguenot Trail run west through Chesterfield and Powhatan counties to US 522 at Jefferson. From near Jefferson, Old River Trail carries on to Michaux.

In 1700 shiploads of French Protestant refugees were sent up the river to 10,000 acres in what is now Powhatan County, at Manakin towne, the largest settlement Huguenots ever made in America. By 1747 their church held its services half in French and half in English.

moments.title: Bellona Arsenal
moments.text: The arsenal that gave Old Gun Road its name stored cannon from 1817, housed a silkworm farm after the Army gave it up, and made cannon for the Confederacy.

moments.title: Huguenot Memorial Chapel
moments.text: The 1895 chapel in the woods off Route 711 rests on a charred beam that may come from the Huguenot church of about 1710, which would make it the nation's oldest Huguenot building fragment.

moments.title: Fine Creek Mills
moments.text: From the 1730s a gristmill worked Fine Creek here. Near its ruins is the site of Fine Creek Manor, where Thomas Jefferson's parents lived a year or two after marrying.
